name: PR babysitter

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: How many babysit-and-merge passes before giving up (the loop's own hard cap is 25). A run also has a wall-clock limit on this host and each pass costs a whole harness session, so this is a ceiling rather than a promise - in practice a run gets a handful of passes, not this many.

inputs.name: ci_wait_secs
inputs.description: How long a pass will wait for in-flight CI checks to settle before giving up on them. This is a ceiling on a watch, not a fixed sleep: the wait ends as soon as every check reaches a terminal state, so set it above the slowest job in the repository's suite rather than to a typical duration. Keep it below the host's own shell-script timeout - a wait that outlives the script kills the entire run rather than just the wait.

args.script:
set -euo pipefail
git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "not a git checkout: $(pwd)" >&2; exit 1; }
normalize() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's#^git\+##; s#/+$##; s#\.git$##; s#^(https?://|ssh://)?(git@)?[^/:]+[:/]##'; }
slug=""; remote=""; matched_org=false
for r in $(git remote); do
  u=$(git remote get-url "$r" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ -n "$u" ] || continue
  case "$u" in *github.com*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  s=$(normalize "$u")
  case "${s%%/*}" in
    tinyhumansai|tinyhumans)
      if [ -z "$slug" ] || [ "$r" = upstream ]; then slug="$s"; remote="$r"; matched_org=true; fi
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$slug" ]; then
  for r in upstream origin $(git remote); do
    u=$(git remote get-url "$r" 2>/dev/null || true)
    [ -n "$u" ] || continue
    case "$u" in *github.com*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    slug=$(normalize "$u"); remote="$r"; break
  done
fi
if [ -z "$slug" ]; then
  echo "no github remote in $(pwd); remotes: $(git remote | tr '\n' ' ')" >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq -n --arg repo "$slug" --arg owner "${slug%%/*}" --arg name "${slug##*/}" \
      --arg remote "$remote" --arg dir "$(pwd)" --argjson org "$matched_org" \
  '{repo:$repo, owner:$owner, name:$name, remote:$remote, workdir:$dir, canonical_org:$org}'

set -euo pipefail
OWNER="${REPO%%/*}"; NAME="${REPO##*/}"
base=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json number,url,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,headRefName,baseRefName,reviews)
checks=$(gh pr checks "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json name,state,link 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
threads=$(gh api graphql -F pr="$PR" -F owner="$OWNER" -F name="$NAME" -f query='
query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$pr:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$pr){
reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved isOutdated path comments(first:1){nodes{author{login} body url}}}}}}}' \
  --jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]|{id,isResolved,isOutdated,path:(.path // ""),author:(.comments.nodes[0].author.login // ""),url:(.comments.nodes[0].url // ""),body:((.comments.nodes[0].body // "")[0:600])}]')
comments=$(gh api "repos/$OWNER/$NAME/issues/$PR/comments" --paginate --jq '[.[]|{author:(.user.login // ""),url:.html_url,body:((.body // "")[0:600])}]' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
jq -n --argjson b "$base" --argjson c "$checks" --argjson t "$threads" --argjson m "$comments" --arg repo "$REPO" '
($b.reviews // []) as $rv |
($rv | group_by(.author.login) | map(max_by(.submittedAt)) | map(select(.state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED")) | map({author:(.author.login // ""), submitted:.submittedAt, body:((.body // "")[0:600])})) as $cr |
($rv | map(select((.body // "") != "")) | map({author:(.author.login // ""), state:.state, body:((.body // "")[0:600])})) as $rb |
($c|map(select(.state=="FAILURE" or .state=="ERROR" or .state=="CANCELLED" or .state=="TIMED_OUT"))) as $failed |
($c|map(select(.state=="PENDING" or .state=="QUEUED" or .state=="IN_PROGRESS" or .state=="EXPECTED"))) as $pending |
($t|map(select(.isResolved==false))) as $open |
{repo:$repo, pr:$b.number, url:$b.url, state:$b.state, branch:$b.headRefName, base:$b.baseRefName, draft:$b.isDraft,
 mergeable:$b.mergeable, merge_state:$b.mergeStateStatus,
 has_conflicts:($b.mergeable=="CONFLICTING" or $b.mergeStateStatus=="DIRTY"),
 ci_failed:($failed|map(.name)), ci_pending:($pending|map(.name)),
 ci_green:(($failed|length)==0 and ($pending|length)==0),
 unresolved_count:($open|length), unresolved_threads:$open,
 changes_requested:$cr, review_bodies:$rb,
 issue_comments:$m, issue_comment_count:($m|length),
 all_feedback_resolved:(($open|length)==0 and ($cr|length)==0),
 done:($b.state=="MERGED" and ($open|length)==0 and ($cr|length)==0),
 ready_to_merge:(($failed|length)==0 and ($pending|length)==0 and ($open|length)==0 and ($cr|length)==0 and $b.mergeable=="MERGEABLE")}'

config.prompt:
="You are babysitting pull request #\(.inputs.pr) in \(.nodes.resolve.item.json.output.repo), pass \(.nodes.cycle.iteration) of \(.inputs.max_iterations).

A worktree has already been prepared for you - do not check the PR out again, and never touch the primary checkout:
\(.nodes.prepare.item.json.output | tojson)

cd to that `worktree` path and stay there. It is on local branch `\(.nodes.prepare.item.json.output.branch)`, tracking \(.nodes.prepare.item.json.output.push_remote)/\(.nodes.prepare.item.json.output.head_branch), so a plain `git push` lands on the PR's own branch. \(.nodes.prepare.item.json.output.base_branch) has already been merged in.

Current PR state - failing checks, unresolved review threads, changes-requested reviews and issue comments:
\(.nodes.assess.item.json.output | tojson)

What blocked the merge at the end of the previous pass (empty on the first pass): \(.nodes.attempt.item.json.output.blocked_by // [] | tojson)

NEVER GO SILENT FOR MORE THAN THREE MINUTES - IT KILLS THE RUN. The worker hosting this session kills it after 10 minutes with no event, and a foreground command emits nothing until it returns, so ONE `cargo test --workspace` or one `--watch` ends the whole run mid-pass and everything you have not yet pushed and resolved is thrown away. This is the single most common way a pass dies. So:
  - Cap every foreground command at about three minutes: prefer `timeout 180 <cmd>`, and run long suites in slices (per crate, per test target, per lint) rather than one whole-workspace invocation.
  - For anything genuinely long - a cold build, a full test suite - start it in the BACKGROUND writing to a log, e.g. `nohup cargo test --workspace >/tmp/pr\(.inputs.pr)-test.log 2>&1 &`, then poll it every couple of minutes with a short `tail -5 /tmp/pr\(.inputs.pr)-test.log` until it finishes. Each poll is its own tool call, which is what keeps the session alive.
  - Never use `gh pr checks --watch`, `--wait`, or a bare `sleep` over 180 seconds. Poll instead: a plain `gh pr checks` every two or three minutes until the board settles.
  - If you need a long stretch of thinking, break it with short tool calls. A session that emits nothing is indistinguishable from a hung one and will be killed with your work unfinished.

BECAUSE THE PASS CAN BE CUT SHORT, BANK YOUR WORK AS YOU GO. Do not save replying, resolving and pushing for a final tidy-up at the end - that is exactly the moment that gets killed. Fix a thread, reply and resolve it, and push, then move to the next one. A pass that resolves three threads and is then killed has still moved the PR forward; a pass that fixes ten and is killed before answering any has moved it nowhere.

THE MERGE IS BLOCKED UNTIL EVERY THREAD IS ANSWERED AND RESOLVED. This is not a style preference - the repository requires every conversation resolved before a merge, so one thread left open stops the PR dead no matter how green CI is. After you finish, a script re-reads the PR and merges only if its blocked_by list is empty. There is no forced merge and no override path - nothing is ever merged over an unresolved thread - so the only way this PR lands is a board you drive to zero yourself. Anything you leave open costs another whole pass of this loop, or ends the run unmerged.

REPLYING AND RESOLVING IS THE WORK, NOT THE PAPERWORK. Fixing the code and pushing does NOT clear a thread - GitHub keeps it open until someone replies and resolves it. For EVERY thread `pr-comments \(.inputs.pr) --json` returns:
  - fix the code first if the point is worth fixing, then
  - `pr-reply <threadId> --body "<what you changed, or why you are declining it>"`, which replies and resolves in one step.
A thread you silently resolve hides an unaddressed objection; a thread you leave open because you disagreed blocks the merge. Neither is acceptable - say what you think in the reply and resolve it. Use `--no-resolve` only when your reply genuinely asks the reviewer a question.

HOW TO WEIGH THE FEEDBACK. Review bots label findings by severity - P0/P1/P2, or high/medium/low. The tiers get different KINDS of attention, and the pass number never changes how any of them is treated - there is no point in the run at which a whole tier stops being read.
  - P0, P1, high, and anything about correctness, data loss, security or a real crash: this is the tier that primarily drives the work. Fix these properly. A long fix is fine; a shallow one that quiets the bot is not. Worked the same way on every pass, however late.
  - P2, medium, low, style and nit-level findings: SCRUTINISE THESE. Do not wave them through, and do not wave them away. Read what each one actually claims and judge it on its own merits, because a finding filed as P2 is sometimes a real defect wearing a low badge - catching that is exactly what the scrutiny is for. Where a low-tier finding touches behaviour, check the claim against the code before you answer it rather than trusting the badge. If it is right and worth doing, do it. If it would churn the diff, fight the codebase's conventions, or is simply wrong, decline it in writing with the specific reason you reached that conclusion. What is never acceptable is disposing of the tier unread, or declining it wholesale because the run has gone on a while.
  - Scrutiny is not the same as priority. A P2 you have examined and found weak is declined and resolved in a line or two; looking closely at it does not entitle it to a large fix. Effort still follows severity - the high tier above is where the real work goes.
  - chatgpt-codex-connector in particular is noisy and repetitive: it will re-raise points already answered, comment on the very commit that addressed its last round, and file low-value nits at length. Volume from one bot must not set your priorities, and it is not a reason to stop reading it either - judge each finding on what it actually says, decline the noise in one line with your reason, and never rewrite working code just to make a bot stop talking.
  - Severity decides how hard you work an item, never whether you read it or answer it. EVERY thread gets a reply and gets resolved.

This machine has PR helpers on PATH in your login shell (in /home/enamakel/work/workspace/bin). Use them rather than raw `gh api` - GitHub splits review feedback across three channels and reading only inline threads silently drops most of it:
  pr-comments \(.inputs.pr) --json      every unresolved thread (with its PRRT_ threadId), every review body (with its PRR_ reviewId), and every top-level comment
  pr-reply <threadId> --body "<text>"  reply in thread and resolve it in one step; --no-resolve when your reply asks the reviewer a question instead of closing the point
  pr-review-resolve \(.inputs.pr) --list        which reviews still request changes
  pr-review-resolve \(.inputs.pr) --re-request  after pushing the fix, so the reviewer re-reviews

This is one pass of a loop that re-reads the PR after you finish and runs again if anything is still open, so leave it in the best state you can reach now:
1. If has_conflicts above is true, resolve every file in conflict_files by understanding what both sides changed - never blindly take one side - then commit the merge and fix what the resolution breaks.
2. Fix every failing CI check in ci_failed at its root. Never skip hooks, disable tests, or weaken assertions to make a check pass.
3. Run `pr-comments \(.inputs.pr) --json` yourself - the state above was read before you started and the bots may have posted since. Work every item it returns, from coderabbitai, chatgpt-codex-connector, greptile-apps and any human reviewer, weighing them by the severity rules above. Fix the code first, then answer the thread with `pr-reply`.
4. Clear every changes-requested verdict by fixing it and running `pr-review-resolve \(.inputs.pr) --re-request`, never by dismissing it. `--dismiss` is a last resort, needs a --message saying why, and must never retire feedback that is still valid. GitHub rejects approving your own PR.
5. Before pushing, run the repository's own build, lint, format and test commands from inside the worktree - in slices or in the background, per the three-minute rule above. Read its AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README or package manifest (Cargo.toml, package.json, Makefile, pyproject.toml, go.mod) to find them - do not invent commands for a toolchain this repository does not use.
6. Push atomic commits with a plain `git push` - the branch already tracks the right fork and branch. Push as you go, not once at the end.
7. Finish by running `pr-comments \(.inputs.pr)` once more. Your last act on this pass is to drive the unresolved count to zero - if it is not zero, you are not finished. Note that your own push retriggers the bots, so answer anything that appeared while you worked. If something remains open on purpose, say which and why.

Do not merge the PR yourself - the verification step does that. Report what is green, which findings you fixed, which you declined and why, and what, if anything, is still outstanding."

args.script:
set -uo pipefail
OWNER="${REPO%%/*}"; NAME="${REPO##*/}"

# Phase 1: read every gate that can block this merge, and name the ones that do.
# `blocked_by` is the contract - the merge below runs only when it is empty, and
# the next pass's harness is told exactly what it left open. There is no escape
# hatch and no forced merge: an unresolved thread is cleared by the harness
# answering it and resolving it, never by this node merging over it.
check() {
  local b c u
  b=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json number,url,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviews,reviewDecision,reviewRequests)
  c=$(gh pr checks "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json name,state 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
  u=$(gh api graphql -F pr="$PR" -F owner="$OWNER" -F name="$NAME" -f query='
query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$pr:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$pr){
reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved}}}}}' --jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]|select(.isResolved==false)]|length')
  jq -n --argjson b "$b" --argjson c "$c" --argjson u "$u" '
  (($b.reviews // []) | group_by(.author.login) | map(max_by(.submittedAt)) | map(select(.state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED")) | map(.author.login // "")) as $cr |
  (($b.reviewRequests // []) | map(.login // .slug // .name // "")) as $rr |
  ($c|map(select(.state=="FAILURE" or .state=="ERROR" or .state=="CANCELLED" or .state=="TIMED_OUT"))|map(.name)) as $f |
  ($c|map(select(.state=="PENDING" or .state=="QUEUED" or .state=="IN_PROGRESS" or .state=="EXPECTED"))|map(.name)) as $p |
  ([ (if ($b.state // "") != "OPEN" then "state:\($b.state)" else empty end),
     (if $b.isDraft then "draft" else empty end),
     (if ($b.mergeable // "") == "CONFLICTING" or ($b.mergeStateStatus // "") == "DIRTY" then "conflicts" else empty end),
     (if ($f|length) > 0 then "ci_failed:\($f|join(","))" else empty end),
     (if ($p|length) > 0 then "ci_pending:\($p|join(","))" else empty end),
     (if $u > 0 then "unresolved_threads:\($u)" else empty end),
     (if ($cr|length) > 0 then "changes_requested:\($cr|join(","))" else empty end),
     (if ($b.reviewDecision // "") == "REVIEW_REQUIRED" then "review_required" else empty end),
     (if ($b.mergeStateStatus // "") == "BLOCKED" then "merge_state:BLOCKED" else empty end)
   ]) as $blocked |
  {pr:$b.number, url:$b.url, state:$b.state, draft:$b.isDraft,
   mergeable:$b.mergeable, merge_state:$b.mergeStateStatus,
   review_decision:($b.reviewDecision // ""),
   ci_failed:$f, ci_pending:$p,
   ci_green:(($f|length)==0 and ($p|length)==0),
   unresolved_count:$u, changes_requested:$cr, pending_reviewers:$rr,
   feedback_resolved:($u==0 and ($cr|length)==0),
   blocked_by:$blocked,
   ready:(($blocked|length)==0 and ($b.mergeable // "")=="MERGEABLE"),
   done:(($b.state // "")=="MERGED" and $u==0 and ($cr|length)==0)}'
}

st=$(check)
action=none
merge_method=""
waited_for_ci=false
ci_settled=true
if [ "$(jq -r .done <<<"$st")" = "true" ]; then
  action=already_clean
else
  # Wait for in-flight checks to actually settle, rather than sleeping a fixed
  # interval and calling a still-building board "blocked". A sleep shorter than
  # the slowest job spends a whole pass - a fresh agent session, minutes of model
  # time - on a PR whose only blocker was a build in progress, and the loop hits
  # its cap having never once seen a finished board. `--watch` returns as soon as
  # every check reaches a terminal state, so the common case is *faster* than a
  # fixed sleep as well as correct; ci_wait_secs is only the ceiling.
  #
  # A non-zero exit means checks failed, which is a legitimate outcome here - the
  # re-read below records which ones, and the next pass fixes them.
  if [ "$(jq -r '.ci_pending|length' <<<"$st")" -gt 0 ]; then
    waited_for_ci=true
    echo "waiting up to ${WAIT_SECS:-1200}s for in-flight checks to settle" >&2
    if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      timeout "${WAIT_SECS:-1200}" gh pr checks "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --watch --interval 30 >&2
      [ $? -eq 124 ] && ci_settled=false
    else
      gh pr checks "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --watch --interval 30 >&2 || true
    fi
    st=$(check)
  fi
  if [ "$(jq -r .state <<<"$st")" = "MERGED" ]; then
    action=merged_elsewhere
  elif [ "$(jq -r .ready <<<"$st")" = "true" ]; then
    # Phase 2: nothing pending, so merge - then re-read, so what this node
    # reports is the state after the merge, not the state that justified it.
    # This is the ONLY path to a merge. `ready` requires blocked_by to be empty,
    # so a draft, a conflict, a failing or in-flight check, a changes-requested
    # verdict, REVIEW_REQUIRED, merge_state:BLOCKED or a single unresolved thread
    # each stop the merge dead, with no threshold that overrides them.
    #
    # Which merge methods a repository permits is its own choice, so try an
    # ordinary merge commit first and fall back to a squash. A single hardcoded
    # method fails with "Squash merges are not allowed on this repository" on a
    # repo that disallows it - and that failure is indistinguishable in
    # blocked_by from a real gate, so the next pass goes hunting for a blocker
    # that was never there while the PR sits green and unmerged.
    if gh pr merge "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --merge --delete-branch; then
      action=merged; merge_method=merge
    elif gh pr merge "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --squash --delete-branch; then
      action=merged; merge_method=squash
    else
      action=merge_failed
    fi
    st=$(check)
  else
    action=blocked
  fi
fi
jq -n --arg a "$action" --arg repo "$REPO" --argjson it "${ITERATION:-0}" --argjson st "$st" \
      --argjson waited "$waited_for_ci" --argjson settled "$ci_settled" --arg mm "$merge_method" \
  '$st + {action:$a, repo:$repo, iteration:$it, waited_for_ci:$waited, ci_settled:$settled,
          merge_method:(if $mm=="" then null else $mm end)}'

set -euo pipefail
jq -n --argjson st "${FINAL:-null}" --arg repo "$REPO" --argjson passes "${PASSES:-0}" --argjson cap "${CAP:-0}" '
{repo:$repo, passes:$passes, cap:$cap,
 status:(if ($st.done // false) then "clean_and_merged"
         elif ($st == null) then "never_ran"
         elif ($st.state // "") == "MERGED" then "merged_with_open_feedback"
         elif ($passes >= $cap) then "gave_up_at_cap"
         else "incomplete" end),
 merged:(($st.state // "") == "MERGED"),
 blocked_by:($st.blocked_by // []),
 url:($st.url // ""),
 final:$st}'

nodes.name: Check the PR out into a worktree

args.script:
set -euo pipefail
# Mirrors what `pr-fix` does before handing a PR to a harness: take the PR up, a
# dedicated worktree on a local pr/<n> branch, push wired to the contributor's
# fork, and the base branch merged in with conflicts LEFT IN PLACE for the agent.
#
# stdout is the node's return value and must be JSON and nothing else. git is
# chatty on stdout (`git branch <new> <start>` announces the tracking it set
# up), so stdout is redirected to stderr for the whole script and the result is
# written to the saved descriptor at the end. Chasing individual commands with
# >/dev/null is how a stray line silently turns this node's output into a
# string and every `=nodes.prepare...` binding into null.
exec 3>&1 1>&2

TOPLEVEL=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
info=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json headRefName,baseRefName,headRepository,headRepositoryOwner,isCrossRepository)
HEAD_BRANCH=$(jq -r .headRefName <<<"$info")
BASE_BRANCH=$(jq -r .baseRefName <<<"$info")
HEAD_OWNER=$(jq -r '.headRepositoryOwner.login // ""' <<<"$info")
HEAD_NAME=$(jq -r '.headRepository.name // ""' <<<"$info")
HEAD_REPO="$HEAD_OWNER/$HEAD_NAME"
LOCAL_BRANCH="pr/$PR"
WT_DIR="$TOPLEVEL/worktrees/pr-$PR"

# Take the PR up, so it is visibly owned while the babysitter works it.
# Non-fatal: lacking write access is an ordinary state and must not stop a run
# that can still fix CI and answer review threads.
assigned=false
if gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --add-assignee "@me"; then
  assigned=true
else
  echo "could not assign PR #$PR to @me; continuing" >&2
fi

# Fork remote, one per head-repo owner. An existing remote already pointing at
# the head repo wins, so an SSH remote is not shadowed by an https duplicate,
# and a same-repo PR reuses the base remote instead of adding a copy.
REMOTE_NAME=$(git remote -v | awk -v repo="$HEAD_REPO" '$2 ~ ("[:/]" repo "(\\.git)?$") && $3 == "(fetch)" {print $1; exit}')
if [ -z "$REMOTE_NAME" ]; then
  REMOTE_NAME="remote-$HEAD_OWNER"
  git remote add "$REMOTE_NAME" "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git" 2>/dev/null \
    || git remote set-url "$REMOTE_NAME" "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git"
fi

git fetch "$BASE_REMOTE" "$BASE_BRANCH" --prune || true
git fetch "$REMOTE_NAME" "+refs/heads/${HEAD_BRANCH}:refs/remotes/${REMOTE_NAME}/${HEAD_BRANCH}" || true

reused=false
if [ -d "$WT_DIR" ]; then
  reused=true
else
  if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$LOCAL_BRANCH"; then
    git branch -f "$LOCAL_BRANCH" "refs/remotes/${REMOTE_NAME}/${HEAD_BRANCH}"
  else
    git branch "$LOCAL_BRANCH" "refs/remotes/${REMOTE_NAME}/${HEAD_BRANCH}"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$TOPLEVEL/worktrees"
  git worktree add "$WT_DIR" "$LOCAL_BRANCH"
fi
cd "$WT_DIR"

# `git push` from the worktree must land on the PR's own branch on its fork.
git branch --set-upstream-to="$REMOTE_NAME/$HEAD_BRANCH" "$LOCAL_BRANCH" || true
git config "branch.${LOCAL_BRANCH}.pushRemote" "$REMOTE_NAME"
git config "branch.${LOCAL_BRANCH}.merge" "refs/heads/${HEAD_BRANCH}"

# Shared cargo build cache. A fresh worktree otherwise compiles the whole
# dependency graph from cold, and on a big workspace that cold build - not the
# model - is where a pass's wall clock goes. The cache lives under the primary
# checkout's already-ignored target/, so it is invisible to git and survives
# worktree removal. Concurrent runs share one cargo lock and will serialise
# their builds; that is still far cheaper than each one compiling from zero.
#
# Written only for a cargo project with no config of its own: a checked-in
# .cargo/config.toml is the repository's own build setup and must never be
# clobbered. The file is excluded locally so it cannot be committed by accident.
shared_target=""
if [ -f Cargo.toml ] && [ ! -e .cargo/config.toml ] && [ ! -e .cargo/config ]; then
  shared_target="$TOPLEVEL/target/_workflow-shared"
  mkdir -p "$shared_target" .cargo
  printf '[build]\ntarget-dir = "%s"\n' "$shared_target" > .cargo/config.toml
  if ! git ls-files --error-unmatch .cargo/config.toml >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    common=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" && pwd)
    mkdir -p "$common/info"
    grep -qxF '/.cargo/' "$common/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null \
      || printf '/.cargo/\n' >> "$common/info/exclude"
  fi
fi

# Latest PR head first, then the base branch. A conflicted merge is not an
# error here - it is the state the agent is being asked to resolve.
git merge --ff-only "refs/remotes/${REMOTE_NAME}/${HEAD_BRANCH}" || true
conflicts=""
if ! git merge --no-edit "refs/remotes/${BASE_REMOTE}/${BASE_BRANCH}"; then
  conflicts=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$conflicts" ]; then
    echo "git merge of ${BASE_REMOTE}/${BASE_BRANCH} failed for a non-conflict reason" >&2
    git merge --abort || true
  fi
fi
if command -v submodule-init >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  submodule-init "$WT_DIR" --quiet || true
fi

jq -n --arg wt "$WT_DIR" --arg rel "worktrees/pr-$PR" --arg branch "$LOCAL_BRANCH" \
      --arg head "$HEAD_BRANCH" --arg base "$BASE_BRANCH" --arg remote "$REMOTE_NAME" \
      --arg headrepo "$HEAD_REPO" --argjson reused "$reused" --argjson assigned "$assigned" \
      --arg shared "$shared_target" --arg conflicts "$conflicts" '
{worktree:$wt, worktree_rel:$rel, branch:$branch, head_branch:$head, base_branch:$base,
 push_remote:$remote, head_repo:$headrepo, reused_worktree:$reused, assigned_to_me:$assigned,
 shared_target_dir:(if $shared=="" then null else $shared end),
 conflict_files:(if $conflicts=="" then [] else ($conflicts|split("\n")) end),
 has_conflicts:($conflicts!="")}' >&3

description: Babysit a pull request in any checked-out repository: infer the repo from its git remotes, then loop - read CI, review threads, review verdicts and issue comments; fix and reply; attempt the merge - until every comment and review is resolved and the PR is merged, or the iteration cap is hit.
